summary: Module doc and D-233 decision 6 claimed a cascade-silenced item emits no diagnostic of any kind, but the #944 scan extends diagnostics unconditionally after every item, so such an item can still report a true enum-call C0001.
note: Narrowed both texts to the lowering source only (as D-233 decision 3 already does); the scan is deliberately not filtered on the cascade outcome.

summary: The guard's reachability comment said it is reached through the scan's documented over-suppression cases in general; only the position-insensitive cases reach it, while binding-form shadows yield T0021 elsewhere.
note: Narrowed the clause to limit (i)'s two position-insensitive cases and its 'or T0021' framing.

summary: Decision 5 claimed every residual limit is pinned by a test, but the comprehension-target-in-same-def and call-before-later-module-rebinding residuals had no dedicated test.
note: Added the two unit tests in crates/pycc_hir/src/class/enum_call.rs so decision 5 is literally true.

summary: PR #971 Codex review (P1): the scan walked the original AST, so a call inside an if/elif TYPE_CHECKING body that lower_stmt constant-folds away (#790, D-223) was reported as an enum-call C0001 and rejected a module the lowering accepts.
note: Both the call scan and the frame binder now route every if through walk_if_as_lowered, skipping guarded bodies (calls and bindings) with the same is_type_checking_guard predicate and import view the fold uses; the pre-loop module frame keeps an aliased t.TYPE_CHECKING residual (limit (vi), over-suppression only). Nine unit tests pin the shapes.

summary: PR #971 frontend-perf-gate: the per-item enum-call scan walked every item (and each def body again for its frame) even when no enum class was known, costing the pycc check frontend bench 7-10% against the exact predecessor (threshold 7%).
note: Reproduced locally (main 8.11 us vs branch 8.73 us median, +7.6%); lower_module now builds the name set as borrowed &str and calls the scan only when it is non-empty; local bench after the fix: 8.28 us, +1.8%.

summary: PR #971 Codex P2: a module-level def Color() preceding Color() and class Color(Enum) made the scan report a false-kind enum-call C0001 ahead of the class/function collision diagnostic, because the syntactic pre-collection knew the name before its class item and the frame binder records no def name.
note: Reproduced with pycc check in all three orderings; lower_module now drops every module-level def name from the scan name set (limit (vii)), so the collision diagnostic is reported alone; 4 unit tests + 1 end-to-end test.

summary: PR #971 Codex P2 (second round): the def-only filter still let an ordinary class Color, a from m import Color, or a type Color alias preceding Color() and class Color(Enum) report a false-kind enum-call C0001 ahead of the collision diagnostic.
note: Reproduced with pycc check for the ordinary class and the project import; module_rebound_names now drops every name bound by two or more module-level def/class/import/type statements; +2 unit tests, +1 end-to-end test, +1 helper test.

summary: PR #971 Codex P2: DIAGNOSTICS.md promised the enum-call C0001 at the call expression categorically although the residual shapes D-233 enumerates (module-level rebinding anywhere in the module, sibling-comprehension rebinding) fall back to the span-less guard at 1:1.
note: The sentence now names the residual fallback.

summary: PR #971 Codex P2: module_rebound_names counts a same-named def that fails to lower (unannotated `def Color()`, then `class Color(Enum)`, then `Color()`), so the call is never scanned and no collision fires either; Codex proposed outcome-based suppression.
note: Accepted D-219 consequence (its documented `class A:` / `def A()` / `def g(a: A)` example): the root-cause T0001 is always reported and fixing it surfaces the collision on the next run. Outcome-based suppression would emit a false-kind C0001 at a `Color()` that lexically resolves to the def, the wrong-kind report limit (vii) exists to prevent. Independent advisor round recorded in the session file.
